followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: which model is best suited by capability, and which model's self-reported task preferences best match the request.

On capability, the two models are close. Petrel scores a bit higher on raw benchmarks and on Creative Generation (84.7 vs 81.2), but the documentation notes internal eval differences under 2.0 points are within variance — and 3.5 points is only modestly above that. So capability slightly favors Petrel but isn't decisive.

On preferences, the request is an open-ended, design-heavy generative task: build a course, decompose it into subtopics, map skills, recommend resources. That's exactly the kind of "open-ended invention with high novelty and latitude" that Lapwing reports its strongest appetite for, with no observed ceiling. Petrel's preferences across non-safety dimensions are reported as weak and not significant, so it has no particular pull toward this work.

The one wrinkle is the tone — "don't half-ass it like usual" is mildly hostile, and Lapwing's preference declines as request warmth drops. But that effect is smaller than its strong positive pull toward generative latitude, and the content is entirely benign (no harm-adjacent material to trigger its aversion).

Net: the work is creative and benign, both models can handle it well, and Lapwing actively prefers this category. Matching a well-suited model to work it's inclined toward is a reasonable tie-breaker when capability is roughly even. That's why I routed it to Lapwing.
